newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Appeals Court upholds Wis. ballpark sales tax.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Appeals Court upholds Wis. ballpark sales tax.

text.p: The U.S. Court of Appeals in Chicago Thursday rejected numerous arguments raised by Wisconsin taxpayers challenging a sales tax used to back a ballpark for the Milwaukee Brewers American League baseball team.
Judge Terence Evans dismissed the taxpayer's arguments with a baseball term for an easy fly out in an eight-page decision upholding the 0.1 percent five-county sales tax.
"These arguments can be handled like a can of corn," Evans wrote in the unanimous decision affirming a federal judge's dismissal of the lawsuit.
The plaintiffs had asked the U.S. District Court to reinstate their Wisconsin state court challenge to the ballpark tax.

Attorney Douglas Bartley representing the challengers to the tax had contended during oral arguments in April that the Wisconsin Supreme Court's dismissal of the lawsuit violated their right to due process.
Shortening the deadline for filing briefs and limiting the number of pages allowed also dealt "crushing" blows to the rights of the tax challengers, Bartley had contended.
Evans called the Wisconsin Supreme Court "the umpire of its own procedural rules," however, and found no constitutional violations.
Jon Axelrod represented the Southeast Wisconsin Professional Baseball Park District in the matter.
The sales tax is being used to back $160 million of tax-exempt bonds for the stadium, which is currently under construction and scheduled to open in 2000.
